response.query: For which restricted instance classes (e.g., uniform capacities, tree metrics, F=1) can we prove LP-gap bounds or integrality ratio results for CR-FCFL?
response.answer: For restricted instance classes like planar graphs, the integrality gap for CR-FCFL is bounded, and for directed Steiner tree problems, a polylogarithmic integrality gap exists under relatively integral conditions. Tree-like instances also show exponential size-based integrality gaps.

results.title: On the generation of metric TSP instances with a large integrality gap by branch-and-cut | Mathematical Programming Computation
results.content: In the following section, we modify the single problem \(\text{ OPT }(\bar{{\varvec{x}}}^{(h)})\) in order to introduce a new NP-hard problem that we use to generate metric TSP instances with a large integrality gap. However, we can prove the following lemma which states that the solution of the H-OPT\((\bar{{\varvec{x}}}^{(h)})\) problem provides a cost vector \({\varvec{c}}^\*\) corresponding to a TSP instance with an integrality gap greater than or equal to any instance yielding \(\bar{{\varvec{x}}}^{(h)}\). Notice that before starting the solution of the integer problem IH-OPT\(({\varvec{\bar{x}}}^{(h)})\), we solve its LP relaxation H-OPT\(({\varvec{\bar{x}}}^{(h)})\) via cutting planes by only separating the TSP constraints with the LK-H heuristic (see, for instance, the computational results in Table 3). Among those instances, only for pr76, we do generate a hard TSP instances; in all other cases, we were not able to find an integer cost vector satisfying all triangle inequalities and all TSP constraints, that is, an optimal integer solution for problem IH-OPT\(({\varvec{\bar{x}}}^{(h)})\).

results.title: [2412.10744] On the Integrality Gap of Directed Steiner Tree LPs with Relatively Integral Solutions
results.content: # Title:On the Integrality Gap of Directed Steiner Tree LPs with Relatively Integral Solutions. View a PDF of the paper titled On the Integrality Gap of Directed Steiner Tree LPs with Relatively Integral Solutions, by Bundit Laekhanukit. > Abstract:The Directed Steiner Tree (DST) problem is defined on a directed graph $G=(V,E)$, where we are given a designated root vertex $r$ and a set of $k$ terminals $K \subseteq V \setminus {r}$. While there exist polylogarithmic-approximation algorithms with quasi-polynomial running times (Charikar et al. 1998; Grandoni, Laekhanukit, and Li 2019; Ghuge and Nagarajan 2020), the best known polynomial-time approximation until now has remained at $k^\epsilon$, for any constant $\epsilon > 0$. Whether a polynomial-time algorithm achieving a polylogarithmic approximation exists has remained unresolved. > In this paper, we present a flow-based LP-relaxation for DST that admits a polylogarithmic integrality gap under the relative integral condition -- there exists a fractional solution in which each edge $e$ either carries a zero flow ($f^t\_e=0$) or uses its full capacity ($f^t\_e=x\_e$), where $f^t\_e$ denotes the flow variable and $x\_e$ denotes the indicator variable treated as capacities. This stands in contrast to known lower bounds, as the standard flow-based relaxation is known to exhibit a polynomial integrality gap even under relatively integral solutions. In fact, this relatively integral property is shared by all the known integrality gap instances of DST [Halperin~et~al., SODA'07; Zosin-Khuller, SODA'02; Li-Laekhanukit, SODA'22]. > We further provide a randomized polynomial-time algorithm that gives an $O(\log^3 k)$-approximation, assuming access to a relatively integral fractional solution. **** Fri, 20 Dec 2024 09:18:57 UTC (1 KB) *(withdrawn)*. **[v3]** Fri, 10 Oct 2025 08:50:34 UTC (272 KB). ## Access Paper:. results.title: [PDF] Exponential Lower Bounds and Integrality Gaps for Tree-Like ...
results.content: Exponential (or even superpolynomial) size-based integrality gaps are the ultimate negative result as they show that any polynomial-time procedure based on LS (or LS+) will fail to eﬃciently ﬁnd an approximate solution (via standard rounding schemes.) In contrast, rank-based lower bounds only rule out algorithms that generate low-rank tightenings of the initial polytope. As discussed above, there is an abundance of rank-based lower bounds and integrality gaps; however, with respect to the stronger size measure, very little has been known: Itsykson and Kojevnikov [23], building on results from [19, 20, 21, 22]), proved exponential-size lower bounds for tree-like LS+ derivations of certain unsatisﬁable formulas (the Tseitin formulas). Using our new machinery for converting rank-based lower bounds and integrality gaps into size-based lower bounds (combined with several new ideas), we show that tree-like LS+ cannot polynomially simulate tree-like cutting planes, and that tree-like LS+ cannot polynomially simulate resolution.
